c.tagline: Gateway to Pakistan's Swat Valley, where Gandhara ruins meet Himalayan foothills.

taxi.fareNote: Formal metered taxis are rare in Mingora; most rides are negotiated in advance with local sedans, Suzuki pickups/vans, or auto-rickshaws, so agreeing on a price before departure is essential.

emergency.note: Rescue 1122 is Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's provincial emergency service covering ambulance, fire, and rescue, and is generally more responsive in Swat than calling police directly.

avoid.reason: Swat — much improved but a former militancy area; check advisories

hood_desc: Mingora's busy central roundabout and commercial hub lined with shops, banks, and traffic; useful as an orientation point but mainly a passthrough rather than a destination in itself.

The adjoining twin town housing the Swat Museum, main hospitals, and government offices, with easy access to the White Palace at nearby Marghazar; best for visitors focused on Gandhara-era history and archaeology.
Mingora's traditional cloth, gem, and embroidery market streets, reflecting the city's long trading role in the Swat Valley; suits travelers wanting local shopping and everyday bazaar life.
A riverside park and picnic area along the Swat River on the edge of town, popular with domestic day-trippers; good for a quieter break and mountain views without leaving the city.
A quieter outlying area near Saidu Sharif Airport and the University of Swat; mainly relevant for its transport links rather than sightseeing.

water.note: Drink only bottled or filtered water.

transit.hours: No fixed schedule; shared vans and rickshaws generally run from early morning until after dark, thinning out late at night.
transit.pay: Cash only, fares agreed informally per seat or per trip; no transit card system exists.
transit.note: Mingora has no formal public transit network; getting around relies on shared Suzuki vans, auto-rickshaws, and hired cars, with fares settled by negotiation.

train: None - Pakistan Railways does not reach Swat
bus: Intercity coaches/vans from Islamabad and Peshawar (e.g., Faisal Movers and local operators)

car.idp: Recommended, though most visitors hire a local car with driver rather than self-driving

airport.name: Saidu Sharif Airport (SDT)

transit.m: Taxi/hired car to city center (20-25 min)

rentals: Local car-with-driver hire only (no international rental chains)

tip.r: Tipping (locally 'baksheesh') isn't obligatory but rounding up or leaving 5-10% at sit-down restaurants and for guides/drivers is customary and appreciated.
